name: Blood Types (Illustrative)
description: A small ABO blood-type sample (n=80) vs. the approximate US distribution. The AB expected count is below 5. Ch. 16 (goodness-of-fit).
studyDescription: A small sample of 80 people had their ABO blood type recorded and compared to the approximate United States distribution (O 44%, A 42%, B 10%, AB 4%). Because AB is rare, its expected count here is only 3.2 — below the 5-per-cell guideline for the chi-square approximation, so a simulation-based test is more trustworthy for this sample.

variableDescriptions.blood_type: A person’s ABO blood type: O, A, B, or AB.

sourceDetail: Illustrative small-sample example (not a specific study), using the approximate U.S. ABO blood-type proportions 0.44 / 0.42 / 0.10 / 0.04. Chosen so the AB expected count (n·0.04 = 3.2) falls below 5 — demonstrating when to prefer the goodness-of-fit simulation over the chi-square approximation.
